references.text: God promises to raise up a prophet who will speak His words, just as Jesus emphasizes that He does not speak on His own authority but speaks what the Father has commanded Him to say.
The Lord promises that His words will be in the prophet's mouth, which mirrors Jesus' claim that the Father has given Him a command regarding what He should speak.
Jeremiah is told that God puts His words into his mouth, a direct parallel to Jesus' statement that He speaks what the Father has commanded Him to say.
Jesus again confirms that He does not speak on His own authority, but that the Father who sent Him has given Him a command regarding what He should say, repeating the theme in John 12:49.
Jesus confirms that the words He has given to the disciples are from the Father, and that He has given them just as the Father gave them to Him, emphasizing that His speech is the Father's command.
